figure.name: George Orwell
figure.role: Writer and democratic socialist focused on political language, propaganda, authoritarian power, and public truth.
figure.hook: Orwell = political language as a tool for truth or evasion.
whyHere: Orwell belongs here because this project is about political words as much as political systems.

He matters because socialism, communism, capitalism, democracy, and freedom can all be used as honest descriptions or as weapons. Orwell helps the study guide ask what a word is doing before accepting it.
figure.cleanIdea: Political language can clarify power, or it can hide responsibility behind slogans, abstractions, and attack labels.

ideas.title: Political Language
ideas.plainDefinition: Political language is the set of words, slogans, categories, and explanations people use to describe power.
ideas.context: In the Orwell path, political language can be a truth tool or a fog machine.
ideas.whyMatters: Political language matters because Hot2Trotski cannot be fair if it lets labels do the thinking.

ideas.title: Propaganda
ideas.plainDefinition: Propaganda is organized communication meant to shape belief, loyalty, fear, or action.
ideas.context: In the Orwell path, propaganda is not only lying. It can also be selective truth, repetition, loaded wording, and category confusion.
ideas.whyMatters: Propaganda matters because political education has to separate evidence from persuasion.

ideas.title: Democratic Socialism
ideas.plainDefinition: Democratic socialism links socialist goals to democracy, civil rights, elections, and public accountability.
ideas.context: In the Orwell path, democratic socialism is a stated political commitment, not a synonym for one-party rule.
ideas.whyMatters: Democratic socialism matters because it prevents the page from collapsing every socialist word into the same historical category.
